key_findings.claim: AlOx Negative Fixed Charge and Its Function
key_findings.detail:
The AlOx layer in PERC cells provides passivation in two ways:

1. **Chemical passivation:** Saturates dangling bonds at the rear Si surface
2. **Field-effect passivation:** The negative fixed charge ($Q_f \approx -10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$) repels minority carriers (holes in p-type Si base) from the rear surface, preventing recombination

Under PID-polarization, positive charge accumulation (Na⁺) neutralizes $Q_f$:

- As $|Q_f|$ decreases, minority carrier repulsion weakens
- Holes flow to the rear surface and recombine at interface defects
- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=2|Chen et al. (2019), p.2]]

Rear passivation loss manifests primarily as Isc and Voc reduction (unlike front-side PID-s, which is FF-dominated):

After 136 h of PID stress at 1000 V, 85°C (bifacial PERC, glass/glass):

- **Rear-side Isc loss:** 28–40%
- **Rear-side Voc loss:** 28–36%
- **Rear-side FF loss:** 37–42%
- **Rear shunt resistance:** Dropped from 162 kΩ·cm² to 0.034–0.044 kΩ·cm²
- [[papers/Elsevier-424-2622-2-s2.0-85065845673-2019-J-Physics of potential induced degradation in bifacial p PERC solar cells.pdf#page=3|Chen et al. (2019), p.3]]

Monofacial PERC (front PID-s only), Rsh decrease after 192 h:

- **Baseline:** 33.55% Rsh decrease
- **Gradient SiNx/SiNxOy/SiOx capping:** 14.06% Rsh decrease (2.4× improvement)
- [[papers/Elsevier-318-1928-2-s2.0-85111494015-2021-J-Suppression of potential induced degradation in monofacial PERC solar cells with gradient designed c.pdf#page=4|Duan et al. (2021), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: SiO₂ Thickness Effect on Charge Dissipation
key_findings.detail:
The tunnel SiO₂ layer between the emitter and the SiNx ARC layer controls PID severity by governing charge dissipation:

- **Thick SiO₂ (9 nm):** Completely blocks electron tunneling; no charge dissipation possible; both SiNx RI = 2.0 and 2.2 show identical rapid PID (10–15% loss in 15 minutes)
- **Thin SiO₂ (1 nm) with high-RI SiNx (n = 2.2):** Electron tunneling dissipates accumulated charge in SiNx; PID nearly eliminated (~1% degradation)
- **Thin SiO₂ (1 nm) with low-RI SiNx (n = 2.0):** No Si-rich SiNx; insufficient electron supply for dissipation; ~10% degradation
- [[papers/Wiley-178-1653-2-s2.0-85127380886-2022-J-Effects of SiNx refractive index and SiO2 thickness on polarization-type potential-induced degradati.pdf#page=3|Wang et al. (2022), p.3]]

Rear passivation loss is partially reversible:

- Light soaking or positive voltage application can partially restore the effective negative charge in AlOx
- Recovery rate increases dramatically with decreasing SiO₂ thickness (when RI is high), confirming tunneling-mediated charge redistribution
- PERC cells recover faster than standard p-type cells from PID-s under comparable conditions
- [[papers/Wiley-178-1653-2-s2.0-85127380886-2022-J-Effects of SiNx refractive index and SiO2 thickness on polarization-type potential-induced degradati.pdf#page=5|Wang et al. (2022), p.5]]
